## Motivation

Valen's complete dense Qwen3.5 checkpoints answer Choice, Noul, and Score
questions using one shared causal prefill and a trained FP32 Mixer. This adds
native checkpoint loading and text/image/video decisions through `/v1/valen`.
All questions read the same processed state and retain the trained role/readout
layout and original answer formulas.

## Modifications

- Register `valen_qwen` and `ValenQwenForDecisionMaking`, reuse Qwen3.5 language
  and vision kernels/fused loaders, and strictly validate backbone and Mixer
  loading. Keep the Mixer parameters and computation in FP32.
- Carry request-local layouts through embedding IPC, scheduling, and forward
  batches. Require TP=PP=1 with complete prefill, disabled radix/chunking/CUDA
  graphs, and explicit errors for unsupported quantization or prompt truncation.
- Preserve Choice order, fixed bilingual Noul descriptions, and 2–255-level
  native Score. Add `/v1/valen` and a limited text/image `/v1/systemone` adapter.
- Use checkpoint HF media settings before appending schema tokens; transfer
  expanded IDs, pixels, and grids as `processor_output`. Preserve the training
  processor's video wrapper semantics with current Transformers. Reuse bounded
  URL loading, count assets before bundling, and clean temporary media on errors.
- Validate reserved controls against tokenizer.json added-token metadata as well
  as the tokenizer's special-token map. Add API documentation and CPU regressions.

## Accuracy Tests

- **39 CPU tests passed, 1 skipped** (37 Valen tests and two neighboring Clef CPU
  tests; the skipped neighboring test requires CUDA). Includes prompt/layout,
  FP32 head math, packed request isolation, media/limit errors, URL staging and
  cleanup, response semantics, and generator lifecycle.
- Ten component cases match the original Valen compiler, role spans, media
  pixels, MRoPE, and answer function. Random shared Mixer weights with FP32/BF16
  hidden inputs: maximum logit error 1.2e-7. Nine cases with the actual released
  2B Mixer weights and random hidden inputs: 1.4e-6. Real SGLang CPU media
  splitting/offset/MRoPE checks passed image, video, and interleaved fixtures.
- **Native GPU validation on one H200**, with complete Valen-2B weights and
  `model_impl=sglang`: strict loading, vision encoding, hybrid GDN/attention,
  pooling, and serving passed eight synthetic text/image/video/mixed multi-turn
  cases, including mixed Choice/Noul/Score questions.
- Original HF reference: FP32 stored backbone + BF16 autocast, PyTorch 2.6 and
  Transformers 5.4. Native runtime: BF16 backbone + FP32 Mixer, PyTorch 2.14.1
  (CUDA 13), Transformers 5.19, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, and FlashInfer 0.7.2.
  Language/GDN attention used Triton; vision used FA3. Prompt IDs matched exactly.

| Full-model comparison to original HF | Maximum absolute error | Smoke tolerance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Probability / Noul | 0.005102 | 0.02 |
| Score | 0.009516 | 0.1 |
| Confidence | 0.014274 | 0.05 |
| Raw candidate logits | 0.439496 | Reported separately |

All Choice decisions matched. These are synthetic correctness checks, not a
workload-level quality evaluation. Raw logits are not bitwise equivalent across
these storage/compute precisions and kernels.

- Concurrent versus isolated native requests: Choice decisions matched; maximum
  probability change 0.007273, below the explicit 0.01 tolerance. Raw logit change
  reached 0.036502 on a soft-label case; the report retains that drift rather
  than claiming identical BF16 reductions across batch shapes.
- **Actual HTTP server**: eight isolated and eight concurrent `/v1/valen`
  requests passed, including image/video/mixed inputs and response token counts.
  A tokenizer.json control-token injection was correctly rejected with 400.
- Ruff/isort/formatting, registered-test lint, diff whitespace, Mintlify build
  validation, and internal link checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No controlled performance benchmark yet. The validation records smoke forward
and HTTP timings, including initial compilation. The HF baseline uses its torch
fallback, so those timings are not presented as a speedup claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Native model/config and trained decision API implemented.
- [x] Text, image, and video frontend parity and CPU CI regressions.
- [x] Complete native weights/backbone/Mixer execution on an H200.
- [x] Original HF comparisons with numerical differences explicitly reported.
- [x] Concurrent requests and actual multimodal HTTP checks.
- [x] API docs, formatting, and Mintlify checks.
- [ ] Broader workload accuracy and controlled performance profiling.
- [ ] Upstream GPU regression registration with checkpoint/fixture availability.

This is a draft for review. Initial supported scope is unquantized dense
Qwen3.5 + Mixer, shared-state execution, TP=PP=1. The tested checkpoint is
Valen-2B; TP/PP, quantization, and other head architectures are outside this PR.

 - The SDKs' `models.list()` and response `request_id` are not supported, because `GET /v1/models` keeps its OpenAI format and no request id header is sent.
 - The SDKs time out after 10 seconds and retry, so raise their timeout for requests with many questions over a long state. A request whose client gives up still finishes its encoding and part of its prefill, so each retry repeats at least the encoding.
 
+## Native Valen decisions
+
+Valen checkpoints with architecture `ValenQwenForDecisionMaking` use a dense
+Qwen3.5 language and vision backbone plus an FP32 Mixer head. All questions share
+one causal prefill. The head pools context, instruction, candidate, and decision
+hidden states and returns candidate scores without generating text.
+
+### Launch Valen
+
+Use Linux with an NVIDIA CUDA GPU and a complete Hugging Face Valen checkpoint
+containing the backbone, vision encoder, Mixer weights, tokenizer, and processor.
+The native path requires `qwen_execution=shared_state`, a Mixer head, tied word
+embeddings, and unquantized weights. The initial configuration uses one GPU with
+TP=1 and PP=1. Video decoding requires FFmpeg shared libraries and TorchCodec,
+as provided by SGLang's CUDA container.
+
+```bash Command
+MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Valen-2B
+python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" --model-impl sglang \
+  --dtype bfloat16 --tp-size 1 --pp-size 1 \
+  --attention-backend triton --linear-attn-backend triton \
+  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
+```
+
+Set BF16 explicitly: released full checkpoints store FP32 backbone weights while
+reference inference uses BF16 autocast. The Mixer retains FP32 parameters and
+computation. Native BF16 kernels can produce slightly different scores from the
+reference implementation.
+
+SGLang detects the Valen architecture and enables embedding mode, disables radix
+reuse and chunked prefill, and disables CUDA graphs. It rejects prompts that
+exceed the checkpoint's `valen_max_length` or the server's effective prefill
+limit, instead of truncating role or readout positions.
+
+### Send text, images, or video
+
+Call `POST /v1/valen` with a text `state`, or a state object containing `messages`.
+Message content accepts text, `image_url`, and `video_url` parts in conversation
+order. Media URLs can be HTTP(S), data URIs, or absolute paths accessible to the
+server. The server's media URL restrictions and asset limits apply.
+
+This example sends a video and shares it across three questions. Set `VIDEO_PATH`
+to a file on the server.
+
+```python Example
+import requests
+
+VIDEO_PATH = "/absolute/path/traffic-light.mp4"
+response = requests.post(
+    "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/valen",
+    json={
+        "state": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
+            {"type": "text", "text": "Observe the final traffic light."},
+            {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": VIDEO_PATH}},
+        ]}]},
+        "questions": {
+            "color": {
+                "type": "choice",
+                "instructions": "What color is the light in the final frame?",
+                "criteria": {"red": "Red light", "green": "Green light"},
+            },
+            "go": {
+                "type": "noul",
+                "instructions": "Crossing is allowed only on green. Is crossing allowed now?",
+            },
+            "risk": {
+                "type": "score",
+                "instructions": "How risky is crossing in the final state?",
+                "criteria": ["Low risk", "Medium risk", "High risk"],
+            },
+        },
+    },
+    timeout=120,
+)
+response.raise_for_status()
+print(response.json()["answers"])
+```
+
+For an image, use `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": IMAGE_URL}}` in
+the content list. For text, set `state` to a string. Multi-turn messages can mix
+images and video. The HF processor uses `valen_media_kwargs` from the checkpoint
+for image resizing and video frame sampling. Its expanded token IDs, pixel
+tensors, and grids enter SGLang together, preserving the trained prompt layout.
+
+### Valen request and response fields
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `state` | Text or an object with a nonempty `messages` list containing the shared context. |
+| `questions` | Nonempty map keyed by your question IDs; IDs key the answers. |
+| `questions[id].instructions` | Required, nonempty question text. |
+| `questions[id].criteria` | For Choice, 1–255 ordered key-to-description entries; for Score, 2–255 ordered descriptions. Descriptions must be nonempty. Noul uses its trained fixed True/False descriptions. |
+| `temperature` | Positive, finite number dividing candidate logits before softmax; default 1. |
+| `model` | Optional model name; the response identifies the served model. Adapter names containing a colon are refused. |
+
+Each answer includes its `type`. Choice returns `choice`, `probabilities`, and
+`confidence`. Noul returns the probability of true in `noul`. Score returns
+`score` as the probability-weighted, zero-based level index, together with
+`probabilities`, `legend`, and `confidence`. These fields use Valen's reference
+formulas. The response also includes `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens`
+(always 0), and `internal_usage.compute_tokens`. Input tokens count the shared
+context and complete question schema once.
+
+The Valen `/v1/systemone` adapter accepts text `state` with optional `images`
+within that route's existing question schema. It requires instructions and
+nonempty Choice descriptions, uses fixed Noul descriptions, and refuses nonempty
+`chat_template_kwargs`. Use `/v1/valen` for message histories, video, or Score
+questions above the System One schema's 10-level limit. Reserved tokenizer
+control tokens in user text are refused. Generation and ordinary embedding
+requests do not return Valen decisions.

 When you need your own prompt or labels, build the prompt on the client and score it through `/v1/score`, which takes token ids and one label list per item. This needs `transformers` and `jinja2` on the client. Every label must be exactly one token at the answer position:

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Compile Valen's trained suffix after an already processed state context.
+
+The media/tokenizer frontend owns the context. Passing its expanded token IDs
+avoids processing images or videos twice and keeps all layout positions final.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
+from copy import deepcopy
+from typing import Any
+
+import msgspec
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.valen_layout import (
+    ValenLayout,
+    ValenQuestionLayout,
+    validate_valen_layout,
+)
+
+NOUL_OPTIONS = (
+    ("true", "True / 是：满足问题中的条件。"),
+    ("false", "False / 否：不满足问题中的条件。"),
+)
+
+
+class ValenQuestion(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    qid: str
+    kind: str
+    keys: tuple[str, ...]
+    descriptions: tuple[str, ...]
+
+
+class ValenEncodedPrompt(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    input_ids: list[int]
+    layout: ValenLayout
+    questions: tuple[ValenQuestion, ...]
+
+
+def _control_tokens(tokenizer):
+    # HF's special-token map can omit controls that are registered as special
+    # only in tokenizer.json (including Qwen's im_start). Consult the added-token
+    # metadata as well, without rejecting ordinary, non-special added words.
+    tokens = set(tokenizer.all_special_tokens)
+    for token in getattr(tokenizer, "added_tokens_decoder", {}).values():
+        if token.special:
+            tokens.add(token.content)
+    return tokens
+
+
+def valen_options(question: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
+    if not isinstance(question, Mapping):
+        raise ValueError("Valen questions must be objects")
+    instructions = question.get("instructions")
+    if not isinstance(instructions, str) or not instructions.strip():
+        raise ValueError("Valen instructions must be nonempty text")
+    kind, criteria = question.get("type"), question.get("criteria")
+    if kind == "noul":
+        return NOUL_OPTIONS
+    if kind == "choice":
+        if not isinstance(criteria, Mapping) or not 1 <= len(criteria) <= 255:
+            raise ValueError("Valen Choice needs 1–255 candidates")
+        options = tuple(criteria.items())
+    elif kind == "score":
+        if not isinstance(criteria, list) or not 2 <= len(criteria) <= 255:
+            raise ValueError("Valen Score needs 2–255 ordered descriptions")
+        options = tuple((str(i), text) for i, text in enumerate(criteria))
+    else:
+        raise ValueError("Unknown Valen question type")
+    if any(
+        not isinstance(key, str)
+        or not key
+        or not isinstance(text, str)
+        or not text.strip()
+        for key, text in options
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Valen candidate keys and descriptions must be nonempty text")
+    return options
+
+
+def encode_valen_schema(
+    tokenizer: Any,
+    context_ids: Sequence[int],
+    questions: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]],
+    max_length: int = 32768,
+) -> ValenEncodedPrompt:
+    if not context_ids or any(
+        type(token) is not int or token < 0 for token in context_ids
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Valen context must contain processed token IDs")
+    if not isinstance(questions, Mapping) or not questions:
+        raise ValueError("Valen needs at least one question")
+    if type(max_length) is not int or max_length < 1:
+        raise ValueError("Valen max_length must be a positive integer")
+    base_length, suffix = len(context_ids), []
+
+    def append(text: str, span: tuple[int, int] | None = None):
+        start = base_length + len(suffix)
+        if span is None:
+            suffix.extend(tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False))
+            return None
+        encoded = tokenizer(text, add_special_tokens=False, return_offsets_mapping=True)
+        suffix.extend(encoded["input_ids"])
+        indices = [
+            i
+            for i, (a, b) in enumerate(encoded["offset_mapping"])
+            if a < span[1] and b > span[0]
+        ]
+        if not indices:
+            raise ValueError("Empty Valen role token span")
+        return start + indices[0], start + indices[-1] + 1
+
+    metadata, layouts = [], []
+    control_tokens = _control_tokens(tokenizer)
+    append("<|im_start|>user\n")
+    for index, (qid, question) in enumerate(questions.items()):
+        options = valen_options(question)
+        for value in (
+            question["instructions"],
+            *(v for option in options for v in option),
+        ):
+            if any(token in value for token in control_tokens):
+                raise ValueError("Reserved tokenizer control token in Valen schema")
+        prefix = f"Question {index + 1}\nTask: {question['type']}\nQuestion: "
+        instruction = append(
+            prefix + question["instructions"] + "\nCandidates:\n",
+            (len(prefix), len(prefix) + len(question["instructions"])),
+        )
+        spans = []
+        for key, description in options:
+            prefix = key + ": " if question["type"] != "score" else ""
+            spans.append(
+                append(
+                    prefix + description, (len(prefix), len(prefix) + len(description))
+                )
+            )
+            append("\n")
+        layouts.append(
+            ValenQuestionLayout(question["type"], instruction, tuple(spans), -1)
+        )
+        metadata.append(
+            ValenQuestion(
+                qid,
+                question["type"],
+                tuple(k for k, _ in options),
+                tuple(v for _, v in options),
+            )
+        )
+    append("<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n")
+    completed = []
+    for index, layout in enumerate(layouts):
+        append(f"Question {index + 1} Decision:")
+        completed.append(
+            ValenQuestionLayout(
+                layout.kind,
+                layout.instruction_span,
+                layout.candidate_spans,
+                base_length + len(suffix) - 1,
+            )
+        )
+        append("\n")
+    ids = list(context_ids) + suffix
+    if len(ids) > max_length:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Valen prompt has {len(ids)} tokens, exceeds max_length={max_length}; no truncation"
+        )
+    layout = ValenLayout(len(ids), (0, base_length), tuple(completed))
+    validate_valen_layout(layout, len(ids))
+    return ValenEncodedPrompt(ids, layout, tuple(metadata))
+
+
+def valen_messages(tokenizer, state, *, allow_media=False):
+    """Normalize state without mutating it or accepting injected control tokens."""
+    control_tokens = _control_tokens(tokenizer)
+    if isinstance(state, str):
+        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": state}]
+    else:
+        messages = deepcopy(state.get("messages"))
+    if not isinstance(messages, list) or not messages:
+        raise ValueError("Valen state needs nonempty messages")
+    for message in messages:
+        if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") not in {
+            "user",
+            "assistant",
+            "system",
+        }:
+            raise ValueError("Unsupported Valen message role")
+        content = message.get("content")
+        if isinstance(content, str):
+            content = [{"type": "text", "text": content}]
+            message["content"] = content
+        if not isinstance(content, list):
+            raise ValueError("Valen message content must be text or a content list")
+        for item in content:
+            if not isinstance(item, dict):
+                raise ValueError("Valen content items must be objects")
+            kind = item.get("type")
+            if allow_media and kind in {"image_url", "video_url"}:
+                source = item.get(kind)
+                url = source.get("url") if isinstance(source, dict) else None
+                if not isinstance(url, str) or not url.strip():
+                    raise ValueError(f"Valen {kind} needs a nonempty url")
+                # HF consumes image/video items; the URL itself is not prompt text.
+                item.clear()
+                item.update(type=kind.removesuffix("_url"), url=url)
+                continue
+            if kind != "text":
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Use the Valen multimodal processor for image/video content"
+                )
+            text = item.get("text")
+            if not isinstance(text, str):
+                raise ValueError("Valen text content must be a string")
+            if any(token in text for token in control_tokens):
+                raise ValueError("Reserved tokenizer control token in Valen state")
+    return messages
+
+
+def encode_valen_text(tokenizer, state):
+    """Match the training compiler's add_generation_prompt=False text context."""
+    messages = valen_messages(tokenizer, state)
+    return tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+        messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=False, return_dict=False
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Bridge Valen's HF processor to SGLang's processor_output media input.
+
+Expand the entire state before appending the independently tokenized schema.
+Passing the resulting pixel tensors and grids avoids a second decode, resize,
+frame sampling or prompt tokenization in SGLang's multimodal processor.
+"""
+
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from copy import deepcopy
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
+from typing import Any
+from urllib.parse import unquote, urlparse
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.valen.encoding import (
+    ValenEncodedPrompt,
+    encode_valen_schema,
+    encode_valen_text,
+    valen_messages,
+)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ValenProcessedPrompt:
+    encoded: ValenEncodedPrompt
+    image_data: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
+    video_data: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _materialize_media(messages):
+    """Use SGLang's bounded URL loader before HF decodes downloaded assets."""
+    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="sglang-valen-") as directory:
+        index = 0
+        for message in messages:
+            for item in message["content"]:
+                if item["type"] == "text":
+                    continue
+                url = item["url"]
+                if url.startswith("file://"):
+                    item["url"] = unquote(urlparse(url).path)
+                elif url.startswith(("http://", "https://", "data:")):
+                    # The common loaders enforce configured domains, redirects,
+                    # byte limits and timeouts. HF must not download again.
+                    from sglang.srt.utils import get_image_bytes, get_video_bytes
+
+                    load = (
+                        get_image_bytes if item["type"] == "image" else get_video_bytes
+                    )
+                    path = Path(directory) / f"{index}.media"
+                    path.write_bytes(load(url))
+                    item["url"] = str(path)
+                    index += 1
+        yield messages
+
+
+def encode_valen_prompt(
+    tokenizer,
+    processor,
+    state,
+    questions,
+    *,
+    media_kwargs,
+    max_length,
+    media_limits=None,
+):
+    messages = valen_messages(tokenizer, state, allow_media=True)
+    # processor_output bundles contain all assets of one modality. Check the
+    # actual asset count before bundling, so the server's media limits still apply.
+    for kind, limit in (media_limits or {}).items():
+        count = sum(item["type"] == kind for m in messages for item in m["content"])
+        if count > limit:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Valen request contains {count} {kind} inputs; server limit is {limit}"
+            )
+    if all(item["type"] == "text" for m in messages for item in m["content"]):
+        return ValenProcessedPrompt(
+            encode_valen_schema(
+                tokenizer,
+                encode_valen_text(tokenizer, state),
+                questions,
+                max_length=max_length,
+            )
+        )
+    if processor is None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Valen image/video requests require the checkpoint's HF processor"
+        )
+    return encode_valen_media(
+        processor, state, questions, media_kwargs=media_kwargs, max_length=max_length
+    )
+
+
+def encode_valen_media(processor, state, questions, *, media_kwargs, max_length):
+    """Use the checkpoint's sampling/resizing settings, as Compiler.compile does."""
+    messages = valen_messages(processor.tokenizer, state, allow_media=True)
+    kwargs = deepcopy(media_kwargs)
+    kwargs["return_metadata"] = True
+    template_kwargs = {}
+    if callable(getattr(processor, "replace_video_token", None)):
+        # The trained HF processor replaced the entire wrapped video marker
+        # with timestamped, individually wrapped frames. Newer HF processors
+        # replace only video_pad, leaving an extra outer pair of vision tokens.
+        # Adapt a request-local template before tokenization: removing tokens
+        # afterwards would also miss BPE merges adjacent to the timestamps.
+        template = processor.chat_template
+        marker = (
+            processor.vision_start_token
+            + processor.video_token
+            + processor.vision_end_token
+        )
+        template_kwargs["chat_template"] = template.replace(
+            marker, processor.video_token
+        )
+    try:
+        with _materialize_media(messages):
+            processed = dict(
+                processor.apply_chat_template(
+                    messages,
+                    tokenize=True,
+                    add_generation_prompt=False,
+                    return_dict=True,
+                    return_tensors="pt",
+                    processor_kwargs=kwargs,
+                    **template_kwargs,
+                )
+            )
+    except (OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unable to process Valen media: {error}") from error
+    context_ids = processed["input_ids"]
+    if context_ids.ndim != 2 or context_ids.shape[0] != 1:
+        raise ValueError("Valen processor must return exactly one state context")
+    encoded = encode_valen_schema(
+        processor.tokenizer, context_ids[0].tolist(), questions, max_length=max_length
+    )
+
+    def payload(kind, feature_key, grid_key):
+        features, grid = processed.get(feature_key), processed.get(grid_key)
+        if features is None and grid is None:
+            return None
+        if not isinstance(features, torch.Tensor) or not isinstance(grid, torch.Tensor):
+            raise ValueError(f"Valen processor returned incomplete {kind} features")
+        return [
+            {
+                "format": "processor_output",
+                "modality": kind,
+                "input_ids": encoded.input_ids,
+                feature_key: features,
+                grid_key: grid,
+            }
+        ]
+
+    images = payload("image", "pixel_values", "image_grid_thw")
+    videos = payload("video", "pixel_values_videos", "video_grid_thw")
+    # Some Qwen processor versions expose temporal spacing. Preserve it when
+    # present so SGLang can compute positions for the already sampled frames.
+    if videos:
+        for name in ("second_per_grid_ts", "video_second_per_grid"):
+            if name in processed:
+                videos[0][name] = processed[name]
+    expected = {
+        item["type"]
+        for m in messages
+        for item in m["content"]
+        if item["type"] != "text"
+    }
+    if ("image" in expected and images is None) or (
+        "video" in expected and videos is None
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Valen processor did not return the requested media features")
+    return ValenProcessedPrompt(encoded, images, videos)
+
+
+def validate_valen_media_payload(obj):
+    """Raw media would resample/re-tokenize an already finalized Valen layout."""
+    if obj.audio_data:
+        raise ValueError("Valen supports image/video inputs, not audio")
+    for group in (obj.image_data, obj.video_data):
+        if group is None:
+            continue
+        items = group if isinstance(group, list) else [group]
+        for item in items:
+            if not isinstance(item, dict) or item.get("format") != "processor_output":
+                raise ValueError("Valen media needs HF processor_output from /v1/valen")
+            if item.get("input_ids") != obj.input_ids:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Valen media token IDs must match the finalized prompt"
+                )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Valen answer fields and confidence formulas."""
+
+import math
+
+import torch
+
+
+def valen_answers(questions, logits, temperature=1.0):
+    """The released Valen answer() formulas, evaluated in FP32."""
+    values = torch.as_tensor(logits, dtype=torch.float32)
+    if values.ndim != 1 or len(values) != sum(len(q.keys) for q in questions):
+        raise ValueError("Valen head did not return one logit per candidate")
+    if not torch.isfinite(values).all():
+        raise ValueError("Valen head returned nonfinite logits")
+    if not math.isfinite(temperature) or temperature <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("Valen temperature must be finite and positive")
+    answers, offset = {}, 0
+    for question in questions:
+        count = len(question.keys)
+        probabilities = (
+            (values[offset : offset + count] / temperature).softmax(-1).tolist()
+        )
+        total = sum(probabilities)
+        probabilities = [p / total for p in probabilities]
+        offset += count
+        result = {"type": question.kind}
+        if question.kind == "noul":
+            result["noul"] = probabilities[question.keys.index("true")]
+        else:
+            result["probabilities"] = dict(zip(question.keys, probabilities))
+            mode = max(range(count), key=probabilities.__getitem__)
+            if question.kind == "choice":
+                result["choice"] = question.keys[mode]
+                result["confidence"] = (
+                    1.0
+                    if count == 1
+                    else max(0.0, (max(probabilities) - 1 / count) / (1 - 1 / count))
+                )
+            else:
+                result["score"] = sum(i * p for i, p in enumerate(probabilities))
+                result["legend"] = dict(zip(question.keys, question.descriptions))
+                distance = sum(p * abs(i - mode) for i, p in enumerate(probabilities))
+                uniform_mad = (
+                    sum(abs(i - (count - 1) / 2) for i in range(count)) / count
+                )
+                result["confidence"] = max(0.0, 1.0 - distance / uniform_mad)
+        answers[question.qid] = result
+    return answers

+class ValenServing:
+    def __init__(self, tokenizer_manager):
+        self.tokenizer_manager = tokenizer_manager
+
+    async def handle_request(self, request: ValenRequest, raw_request=None):
+        manager = self.tokenizer_manager
+        try:
+            if not manager.model_config.is_valen:
+                raise ValueError("/v1/valen requires a Valen checkpoint")

+                raise ValueError("Valen requires the server tokenizer")
+            if request.model and ":" in request.model:
+                raise ValueError("Valen adapter requests are not supported")
+            limit = min(
+                manager.model_config.hf_config.valen_max_length,
+                max_joint_prompt_tokens(
+                    context_len=manager.context_len,
+                    num_reserved_tokens=manager.num_reserved_tokens,
+                    max_req_input_len=manager.max_req_input_len,
+                    max_prefill_tokens=get_schedule().max_prefill_tokens,
+                ),
+            )
+            media_limits = get_mm().limit_mm_data_per_request
+
+            def compile_request():
+                return encode_valen_prompt(
+                    manager.tokenizer,
+                    getattr(manager, "processor", None),
+                    request.state,
+                    {qid: q.model_dump() for qid, q in request.questions.items()},
+                    media_kwargs=manager.model_config.hf_config.valen_media_kwargs,
+                    max_length=limit,
+                    media_limits=media_limits,
+                )

+            processed = await asyncio.to_thread(compile_request)
+            encoded = processed.encoded
+            obj = EmbeddingReqInput(
+                input_ids=encoded.input_ids,
+                valen_layout=pack_valen_layout(encoded.layout),
+                image_data=processed.image_data,
+                video_data=processed.video_data,
+            )
+            async with aclosing(manager.generate_request(obj, raw_request)) as results:
+                result = await results.__anext__()
+            answers = valen_answers(
+                encoded.questions, result["embedding"], request.temperature
+            )
+            tokens = result["meta_info"]["prompt_tokens"]
+            return ORJSONResponse(
+                content={
+                    "model": manager.served_model_name,
+                    "answers": answers,
+                    "usage": {"input_tokens": tokens, "output_tokens": 0},
+                    "internal_usage": {"compute_tokens": tokens},
+                }
+            )
+        except ValueError as error:
+            return ORJSONResponse(
+                status_code=400,
+                content={
+                    "error": {
+                        "message": str(error),
+                        "type": "invalid_request_error",
+                        "code": 400,
+                    }
+                },
+            )
+
+    async def handle_systemone(self, request, raw_request=None):
+        try:
+            if request.chat_template_kwargs:

+                )
+            if not isinstance(request.state, str):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Use /v1/valen for Valen messages; System One state must be text"
+                )
+            questions = {}
+            for qid, q in request.questions.items():
+                item = q.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
+                if q.type == "noul" and q.criteria is not None:
+                    if any(v is not None for v in q.criteria.model_dump().values()):

+                content={
+                    "error": {
+                        "message": str(error),
+                        "type": "invalid_request_error",
+                        "code": 400,
+                    }
+                },

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Versioned, request-local readouts for Valen shared-state inference."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Sequence, Tuple
+
+import msgspec
+
+QUESTION_TYPES = ("choice", "noul", "score")
+LAYOUT_VERSION = 1
+
+
+class ValenQuestionLayout(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    kind: str
+    instruction_span: Tuple[int, int]
+    candidate_spans: Tuple[Tuple[int, int], ...]
+    decision_position: int
+
+
+class ValenLayout(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    prompt_length: int
+    context_span: Tuple[int, int]
+    questions: Tuple[ValenQuestionLayout, ...]
+
+
+def validate_valen_layout(layout: ValenLayout, num_tokens: int) -> None:
+    """Reject truncated, overlapping or mismatched layouts before scheduling.
+
+    Positions address the final, expanded sequence. Unlike Clef's layout,
+    the context span includes media tokens and must never be shifted whole.
+    """
+    if type(num_tokens) is not int or num_tokens < 1:
+        raise ValueError("Valen needs a nonempty prompt")
+    if layout.prompt_length != num_tokens:
+        raise ValueError("Valen layout does not match the final prompt length")
+    start, end = layout.context_span
+    if start != 0 or not 0 < end < num_tokens:
+        raise ValueError("Invalid Valen context span")
+    if not layout.questions or len(layout.questions) > num_tokens:
+        raise ValueError("Invalid Valen question count")
+    schema_end = end
+    for question in layout.questions:
+        if question.kind not in QUESTION_TYPES:
+            raise ValueError("Unknown Valen question type")
+        count = len(question.candidate_spans)
+        minimum = 1 if question.kind == "choice" else 2
+        if not minimum <= count <= 255 or (question.kind == "noul" and count != 2):
+            raise ValueError("Invalid Valen candidate count")
+        a, b = question.instruction_span
+        if not schema_end <= a < b <= num_tokens:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid or overlapping Valen instruction span")
+        schema_end = b
+        for a, b in question.candidate_spans:
+            if not schema_end <= a < b <= num_tokens:
+                raise ValueError("Invalid or overlapping Valen candidate span")
+            schema_end = b
+    last_decision = schema_end - 1
+    for question in layout.questions:
+        if not last_decision < question.decision_position < num_tokens:
+            raise ValueError("Valen readouts must follow all schemas in order")
+        last_decision = question.decision_position
+

+def pack_valen_layout(layout: ValenLayout) -> list[int]:
+    """Compact IPC representation; independent of Clef's decision_layout."""
+    validate_valen_layout(layout, layout.prompt_length)
+    values = [
+        LAYOUT_VERSION,
+        layout.prompt_length,
+        *layout.context_span,
+        len(layout.questions),
+    ]
+    for question in layout.questions:
+        values.extend(
+            (
+                QUESTION_TYPES.index(question.kind),
+                *question.instruction_span,
+                question.decision_position,
+                len(question.candidate_spans),
+            )
+        )
+        for span in question.candidate_spans:
+            values.extend(span)
+    return values
+
+
+def parse_valen_layout(values: Sequence[int], num_tokens: int) -> ValenLayout:
+    if len(values) < 5 or any(type(value) is not int for value in values):
+        raise ValueError("Valen layout must be a list of integers")
+    version, prompt_length, start, end, count = values[:5]
+    if version != LAYOUT_VERSION:
+        raise ValueError("Unsupported Valen layout version")
+    if prompt_length != num_tokens or not 1 <= count <= num_tokens:
+        raise ValueError("Valen layout does not match the final prompt length")
+    cursor, questions = 5, []
+    for _ in range(count):
+        if cursor + 5 > len(values):
+            raise ValueError("Truncated Valen question layout")
+        kind, a, b, decision, options = values[cursor : cursor + 5]
+        cursor += 5
+        if not 0 <= kind < len(QUESTION_TYPES) or not 1 <= options <= 255:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid Valen question layout")
+        if cursor + 2 * options > len(values):
+            raise ValueError("Truncated Valen candidate layout")
+        spans = tuple(
+            (values[i], values[i + 1]) for i in range(cursor, cursor + 2 * options, 2)
+        )
+        cursor += 2 * options
+        questions.append(
+            ValenQuestionLayout(QUESTION_TYPES[kind], (a, b), spans, decision)
+        )
+    if cursor != len(values):
+        raise ValueError("Valen layout has trailing values")
+    layout = ValenLayout(prompt_length, (start, end), tuple(questions))
+    validate_valen_layout(layout, num_tokens)
+    return layout
+
+
+def rebase_valen_context(layout: ValenLayout, context_length: int) -> ValenLayout:
+    """Expand a prefix context without shifting its start or pooling padding.
+
+    Call only when preprocessing changes the prefix and preserves the schema
+    suffix token-for-token. This is not a replacement for video/MRoPE validation.
+    """
+    validate_valen_layout(layout, layout.prompt_length)
+    if type(context_length) is not int or context_length < layout.context_span[1]:
+        raise ValueError("Valen context expansion cannot remove tokens")
+    shift = context_length - layout.context_span[1]
+    questions = tuple(
+        ValenQuestionLayout(
+            q.kind,
+            tuple(p + shift for p in q.instruction_span),
+            tuple((a + shift, b + shift) for a, b in q.candidate_spans),
+            q.decision_position + shift,
+        )
+        for q in layout.questions
+    )
+    result = ValenLayout(layout.prompt_length + shift, (0, context_length), questions)
+    validate_valen_layout(result, result.prompt_length)
+    return result

+"""Valen's FP32 four-role Mixer, with checkpoint-compatible parameter names."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Sequence
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.valen_layout import ValenLayout, validate_valen_layout

+
+class ValenMixerBlock(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, width: int, token_hidden: int, channel_hidden: int):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.token_norm = nn.LayerNorm(width)
+        self.token_mlp = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(4, token_hidden), nn.GELU(), nn.Linear(token_hidden, 4)
+        )
+        self.channel_norm = nn.LayerNorm(width)
+        self.channel_mlp = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(width, channel_hidden),
+            nn.GELU(),
+            nn.Linear(channel_hidden, width),
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        x = x + self.token_mlp(self.token_norm(x).transpose(1, 2)).transpose(1, 2)
+        return x + self.channel_mlp(self.channel_norm(x))
+
+
+class ValenMixerHead(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        hidden_size: int,
+        head_width: int = 256,
+        head_layers: int = 2,
+        head_token_hidden_dim: int = 16,
+        head_channel_hidden_dim: int = 1024,
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        if any(
+            type(v) is not int or v < 1
+            for v in (
+                hidden_size,
+                head_width,
+                head_layers,
+                head_token_hidden_dim,
+                head_channel_hidden_dim,
+            )
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Valen Mixer dimensions must be positive integers")
+        self.input_norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.projection = nn.Linear(hidden_size, head_width)
+        self.roles = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, 4, head_width))
+        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(
+            *(
+                ValenMixerBlock(
+                    head_width, head_token_hidden_dim, head_channel_hidden_dim
+                )
+                for _ in range(head_layers)
+            )
+        )
+        self.output = nn.Sequential(nn.LayerNorm(head_width), nn.Linear(head_width, 1))
+        # SGLang may construct models under a BF16 default dtype.
+        self.float()
+
+    def score_features(self, features: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if features.ndim != 3 or features.shape[1:] != (
+            4,
+            self.input_norm.normalized_shape[0],
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Expected Valen candidate features shaped [N, 4, hidden_size]"
+            )
+        # A surrounding BF16 autocast must not cast Mixer projections.
+        with torch.autocast(device_type=features.device.type, enabled=False):
+            x = self.projection(self.input_norm(features.float())) + self.roles
+            return self.output(self.blocks(x)[:, 2]).squeeze(-1)
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def forward_batch(
+        self,
+        hidden: torch.Tensor,
+        lengths: Sequence[int],
+        layouts: Sequence[ValenLayout],
+    ) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+        """Read packed, uncached prefill rows; return candidate logits per request."""
+        if hidden.ndim != 2 or hidden.shape[1] != self.input_norm.normalized_shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Expected packed hidden states shaped [tokens, hidden_size]"
+            )
+        if len(lengths) != len(layouts) or any(
+            type(n) is not int or n < 1 for n in lengths
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Valen request lengths and layouts do not match")
+        if sum(lengths) != hidden.shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Valen packed hidden states include missing or extra tokens"
+            )
+        if not layouts:
+            return []
+        features, counts, offset = [], [], 0
+        for length, layout in zip(lengths, layouts):
+            validate_valen_layout(layout, length)
+            row = hidden[offset : offset + length]
+            a, b = layout.context_span
+            context = row[a:b].float().mean(0)
+            count = 0
+            for question in layout.questions:
+                a, b = question.instruction_span
+                instruction = row[a:b].float().mean(0)
+                decision = row[question.decision_position].float()
+                for a, b in question.candidate_spans:
+                    candidate = row[a:b].float().mean(0)
+                    features.append(
+                        torch.stack((context, instruction, candidate, decision))
+                    )
+                    count += 1
+            counts.append(count)
+            offset += length
+        return list(self.score_features(torch.stack(features)).split(counts))

+class ValenMixerPooler(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, head: ValenMixerHead):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.head = head
+
+    def forward(
+        self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor, forward_batch
+    ) -> EmbeddingPoolerOutput:
+        lengths = forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu
+        outputs = [
+            hidden_states.new_empty(0, dtype=torch.float32)
+            for _ in range(forward_batch.batch_size)
+        ]
+        if lengths is None or forward_batch.valen_layouts is None:
+            return EmbeddingPoolerOutput(embeddings=outputs)
+        lengths = list(lengths)
+        prefixes = forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens_cpu or [0] * len(lengths)
+        offsets = [0]
+        for length in lengths:
+            offsets.append(offsets[-1] + length)
+        runs, layouts = [], {}
+        for i, (raw, prefix, length) in enumerate(
+            zip(forward_batch.valen_layouts, prefixes, lengths)
+        ):
+            if raw is None or prefix != 0:
+                continue
+            try:
+                layouts[i] = parse_valen_layout(raw, length)
+            except ValueError:
+                # A malformed/truncated request must not kill its batch neighbors.
+                continue
+            if runs and runs[-1][-1] == i - 1:
+                runs[-1].append(i)
+            else:
+                runs.append([i])
+        for run in runs:
+            scores = self.head.forward_batch(
+                hidden_states[offsets[run[0]] : offsets[run[-1] + 1]],
+                [lengths[i] for i in run],
+                [layouts[i] for i in run],
+            )

+                outputs[i] = values
+        return EmbeddingPoolerOutput(embeddings=outputs)

+    def __init__(self, config, quant_config=None, prefix=""):
+        if quant_config is not None:
+            raise ValueError("Valen quantized serving has not been validated")
+        if (
+            config.qwen_execution != "shared_state"
+            or config.valen_head.get("head_type") != "mixer"
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Valen requires shared_state execution with a Mixer head")
+        if not config.tie_word_embeddings:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Valen serving requires the released tied-embedding Qwen3.5 backbone"
+            )
+        super().__init__(config, quant_config=quant_config, prefix=prefix)
+        settings = {
+            key: value for key, value in config.valen_head.items() if key != "head_type"
+        }
+        self.pooler = ValenMixerPooler(
+            ValenMixerHead(config.text_config.hidden_size, **settings)
+        )
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]):
+        head_weights = {}
+
+        def backbone_weights():
+            for name, tensor in weights:
+                if name.startswith("head."):
+                    head_weights[name.removeprefix("head.")] = tensor
+                elif name.startswith("backbone.language_model."):
+                    # Use the conditional model's path, not its bare-backbone
+                    # path (which expects an unrelated LM decision readout).
+                    yield (
+                        "model.language_model."
+                        + name.removeprefix("backbone.language_model."),
+                        tensor,
+                    )
+                elif name.startswith("backbone.visual."):
+                    yield (
+                        "model.visual." + name.removeprefix("backbone.visual."),
+                        tensor,
+                    )
+                else:
+                    raise ValueError(f"Unexpected Valen checkpoint tensor: {name}")
+
+        loaded = super().load_weights(backbone_weights())
+        self.pooler.head.load_state_dict(head_weights, strict=True)
+        loaded.update(
+            f"pooler.head.{name}" for name, _ in self.pooler.head.named_parameters()
+        )
+        expected = {
+            name
+            for name, _ in self.named_parameters()
+            if not name.startswith("lm_head.")
+        }
+        missing = expected - loaded
+        if missing:
+            raise ValueError(f"Incomplete Valen backbone load: {sorted(missing)}")
+        return loaded
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids,
+        positions,
+        forward_batch,
+        get_embedding=False,
+        pp_proxy_tensors=None,
+    ):
+        if not get_embedding:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Valen returns decisions through /v1/valen or /v1/systemone"
+            )
+        return super().forward(
+            input_ids,
+            positions,
+            forward_batch,
+            get_embedding=True,
+            pp_proxy_tensors=pp_proxy_tensors,
+        )
+
+
